title: 2015 Mathematical Contest in Modeling Summary Sheet: Ebola Models and Drug Delivery

limitations: All 34 pages reviewed through rendered contact sheets.
OCR damages Greek symbols and indexed variables; rendered equations are authoritative.
The paper uses capital-city proxies and estimated factors for operational decisions.

task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction, Model I-III, extension, sensitivity, conclusion, and WMA letter
deliverables: Fit SEIR, isolation-aware SEIIR, and effective-medication epidemic models.
Choose medical-center count and locations under a 24-hour coverage constraint.
Rank drug demand from eight contextual factors with TOPSIS.
Model logistic production and optimize allocation in shortage and sufficient regimes.
Extend to vaccine intervention and test sensitivity to transmission, initial state, and production capacity.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No separate official problem statement was located; author prose reconstructs deliverables and does not reclassify the path-derived A label.

section_map.summary: Three model blocks: epidemic phases, facility location, and production/allocation.
Problem background, work route, symbols, assumptions.
SEIR, isolation, medication, and country curves.
Set covering, multiobjective centers, TOPSIS demand factors.
Vaccine extension, initial-state and production sensitivity.

contributions.summary: Early outbreak curves are fitted for three countries.
Isolation splits infectious people into free and isolated paths.
A set-covering multiobjective model chooses medical centers.
Logistic output separates shortage and sufficient supply.

dependency_graph.closure_status: Epidemic states -> facility coverage -> demand ranking -> production -> regime-specific allocation -> policy letter.

assumptions.summary: Population is constant and natural demography is ignored.
Isolated patients do not infect susceptibles.
Centers are at first-level administrative capitals and patients must reach one within 24 hours.
One drug portion represents one complete treatment for a non-advanced patient.
Vaccine is excluded from main allocation optimization and later added symbolically.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: WHO cumulative cases/deaths and literature durations parameterize SEIR.
Google map shortest paths connect Sierra Leone capital proxies.
Density, temperature, humidity, infection, open centers, economy, education, and age become factors.
Factor matrix is normalized before ideal-distance ranking.

verification.summary: Country curves are compared with WHO data.
Isolation trajectory shows blockage of spread.
Seven center solution is plotted on a map.
Gm threshold changes control time and deaths.

results_trace.summary: Seven centers are selected in Sierra Leone.
Logistic capacity reaches Gm around the modeled horizon.
Drug portions are updated every 14 days.
Daily output below 4000 doses cannot control the modeled epidemic.

writing_logic.summary: Three periods -> three model blocks -> six-month plan -> threshold.
Crisis -> drug need -> model route -> delivery decomposition.
Coverage -> facility optimization -> demand factors -> TOPSIS.
Logistic capacity -> shortage/sufficient objectives -> six-month plan.
Public-health controls -> shortage allocation -> sufficient-stage deaths.

language_observations.summary: First/Then/Finally sequence the three model blocks.
A contrast sentence turns baseline fit into an isolation extension.
Optimization family is named before symbols and solution.
Shortage and sufficient regimes receive different objectives.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A visible model-to-policy chain and six-month plan may aid auditability; award status is not causal evidence.

weaknesses.summary: Estimated parameters and mutation can weaken forecast validity.
Capital proxies and shortest-distance simplification omit local geography.
Vaccine is excluded from the main optimization.
The 4000-dose threshold is scenario-dependent and lacks uncertainty.
WMA recommendations lack external operational validation.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace capital proxies with road-time, capacity, stock, and rural-access constraints.
Jointly calibrate beta, E0, logistic r/Gm, vaccine efficacy, and allocation uncertainty.

unresolved_questions: SEIR/SEIIR initial states and estimated factors are not fully reproducible.
The isolation-mortality relation and effective medication flow M(t) are stylized.
Facility capacity, road disruption, and exact multiobjective weighting are absent.
TOPSIS factor weights, proxy direction, and missing-data treatment are incomplete.
Logistic production lacks factory capacity, inventory balance, lead time, and losses.
Shortage/sufficient optimization solver settings and vaccine allocation are not fully specified.
The 4000-dose control threshold is scenario-bound and no external validation is reported.
